blocks.explanation:
\(\tan^2 x\) ka seedha integral hamari list mein nahi, lekin identity \(1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x\) hamari madad karti hai.
Diya hai \(\int x\tan^2 x\,dx\), find karna hai is ka integral.
\(\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1\) likhne se do integrals bante hain: \(\int x\sec^2 x\,dx\) (bilkul Example 31) aur \(\int x\,dx\) (bohat aasaan).
Plan: identity, phir parts sirf pehle hisse par.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int x\tan^2 x\,dx\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: identity \(\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1\); phir parts, \(x\) first aur \(\sec^2 x\) second.

Identity lagayein
\[\int x(\sec^2 x - 1)\,dx\]
\[= \int x\sec^2 x\,dx - \int x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x\) se \(\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1\). Ab ek mushkil integral do jaane pehchane integrals mein toot gaya.

Pehle integral par parts
\[\int x\sec^2 x\,dx = x\tan x - \int \tan x\,dx\]
\[= x\tan x - \ln|\sec x|\]
Kyun: \(\sec^2 x\) ka integral \(\tan x\), \(x\) ka derivative 1. Phir \(\int \tan x\,dx = \ln|\sec x| + c\) wala standard result.

Jor dein
\[= x\tan x - \ln|\sec x| - \dfrac{x^2}{2} + c\]
Kyun: doosra integral \(\int x\,dx = \frac{x^2}{2}\), minus ke saath. Ek hi constant \(c\) aakhir mein.
Dhyan dein: \(-\int x\,dx\) wala hissa bhool jana aam ghalti hai; identity ka \(-1\) bhi \(x\) se zarb hota hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ldots) = \tan x + x\sec^2 x - \tan x - x\]
\[= x(\sec^2 x - 1) = x\tan^2 x\]
Kyun: \(\ln|\sec x|\) ka derivative \(\frac{\sec x\tan x}{\sec x} = \tan x\). \(\tan x\) cancel ho kar integrand wapas mila.
